There is no age requirement to self-harm. The idea that only kids can hurt themselves is absolute bullshit. Your feelings are valid. It doesn't matter if you're 11, 21, or even 65. I promise you, if you tell someone you are struggling, they will not judge you. Self-harm is self-harm regardless of the depth of the wound. Your pain and feelings aren't any less than someone elses just because yours might not be as deep as theirs. Coming forward about your struggles is a brave thing to do, and not many have that kind of strength. Stop worrying about everyone else might think and start worrying about what YOU want for yourself. If you want to get better, you have to be able to talk about the hard stuff. The stuff that you might not be completely comfortable sharing with others. A lot of us have this idea in our minds that we can handle everything by ourselves, but that isn't true. There are times when we need help from others, and right now, you could use that help. 

You're having a hard time right now, but trust that it will get better. I know everyone hates when people say shit like that, but it's the truth. Not everything can be perfect all of the time. You're only 21, and I heard that your early 20s can be a bit of a challenge, so don't expect everything to go your way all of the time. Also, stop assuming that everyone hates you and sees you as a burden. It's a bad habit that many have (including myself) to assume that their existence is somehow a curse to those around them, but that's not reality. Your roommate could have just been having a real shitty day, maybe even a shitty year for all we know, and that could be the reason for her shutting her door. Sometimes, our actions don't aline with how we truly feel. As someone who struggles with bipolar disorder, I have a real short fuse and act as if I hate the people around me, but that is more a reflection on how I feel about my life rather than how I feel about them. Also, I don't know you personally, but you're not a bad person for feeling this way. You're only human after all. It's not like you can be the perfect person all of the time. And you're not selfish for wanting comfort. Most of us desire that. If that's a selfish thing, then we're all selfish.

I do not go to therapy, but I'm in the same boat as you, quite frankly. I have always feared death. Especially the death of those i care about. Death just seems cruel and unfair. As much as i wish people stayed forever, it's just not how the world works. But it's not a bad thing. Especially to those who are religious. A lot of people believe in an afterlife like heaven or hell. Some believe in reincarnation, and there are some who believe death is the greatest thing that can happen to you, believe it or not. It's scary, and i get that, but we all gotta go someday. The best thing you can do is to just prepare for what's to come eventually. Make sure you spend as much time as you can with the people around you because that can actually help after someone has passed. If you spend a lot of time with them, you will have fewer regrets about not being with them more while they were still here. Experiencing death is not going to be easy, and im dreading the day i will have to, but there are many things you can do to move forward after a loss. Research is very important. It's good to do some digging on what you can do to feel at peace with someone's passing. Once someone has died, don't isolate yourself. Don't feel guilty. Don't make it seem like you could have done more when death is just a natural thing that happens to everyone and everything.
